source_text: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ ἐπισκόπους καλουμένους εἰς σύνοδον καταφρονεῖν, ἀλλ᾽ ἀπιέναι, καὶ διδάσκειν, ἢ διδάσκεσθαι, εἰς κατόρθωσιν τῆς ἐκκλησίας καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν. Εἰ δὲ καταφρονήσειεν ὁ τοιοῦτος, ἐαυτὸν αἰτιάσεται, παρεκτὸς εἰ μὴ δι᾽ ἀνωμαλίαν ἀπολιμπάνοιτο.
thought_title: Bishops must not despise a synod summons
orientation: The council is issuing its own decrees, and this canon addresses bishops who are called to a synod.
pass_a_gloss: That it is not right for bishops called to a synod to despise it, but to go away, and to teach, or to be taught, for the correction of the church and of the rest. But if such a one should despise it, he will blame himself, unless he should be absent because of irregularity.

choices.why: The participle with prepositional phrase indicates the summons; 'called to a synod' keeps the passive force and the destination.
The verb means to think little of or disregard; 'despise' preserves the strong negative attitude toward the summons.
The infinitive means to depart or go off; 'go away' keeps the motion away from one's place toward the synod.
The noun means setting right or improvement; 'correction' fits the purpose of the synod for the church and the rest.
The noun means unevenness or anomaly; 'irregularity' renders the exceptional circumstance that excuses absence.
The future middle of αἰτιάομαι with reflexive pronoun means he will hold himself responsible; the rendering keeps the reflexive blame.
rejected: he will have himself to blame

pass_b_english: Bishops who are called to a synod must not despise the summons. They are to go, and to teach or be taught, for the correction of the church and of the rest. If such a bishop despises the summons, he will blame himself—unless he is prevented by illness.

problems.quote: unless he stays away because of some irregularity
problems.source_quote: παρεκτὸς εἰ μὴ δι᾽ ἀνωμαλίαν ἀπολιμπάνοιτο
problems.why: ἀπολιμπάνοιτο is optative of exemption, not 'stays away'; 'irregularity' is weak for ἀνωμαλίαν (illness/infirmity).
problems.fix: except if he be prevented by illness
problems.ruling: ἀνωμαλίαν means bodily infirmity/illness here; 'irregularity' misleads readers about the exemption ground.

edits.old: unless he stays away because of some irregularity
edits.new: except if he be prevented by illness

fixed: Corrected 'unless he stays away because of some irregularity' to 'except if he be prevented by illness': the source optative ἀπολιμπάνοιτο expresses exemption, not staying away, and ἀνωμαλίαν here means illness/infirmity.

problems.quote: except if he be prevented by illness
problems.source_quote: παρεκτὸς εἰ μὴ δι᾽ ἀνωμαλίαν ἀπολιμπάνοιτο
problems.why: ἀνωμαλίαν means irregularity/unevenness, not illness; ἀπολιμπάνοιτο is middle "is left behind/absent", not passive "prevented".
problems.fix: unless he is absent due to some irregularity
problems.ruling: ἀνωμαλίαν = irregularity/unevenness, not illness; ἀπολιμπάνοιτο = left behind/absent, not 'prevented'. Meaning changed.

problems.quote: unless he is absent due to some irregularity
problems.source_quote: παρεκτὸς εἰ μὴ δι᾽ ἀνωμαλίαν ἀπολιμπάνοιτο
problems.why: ἀπολιμπάνοιτο is passive "is left behind/left out," not active "is absent"; ἀνωμαλίαν means unevenness/illness/infirmity, not "irregularity."
problems.fix: unless he is prevented by illness
problems.ruling: ἀνωμαλίαν means illness/infirmity; ἀπολιμπάνοιτο passive = 'is detained/left behind', not active 'is absent'.

edits.new: unless he is prevented by illness

last_rejected.quote: unless he is prevented by illness
last_rejected.source_quote: παρεκτὸς εἰ μὴ δι᾽ ἀνωμαλίαν ἀπολιμπάνοιτο
last_rejected.why: ἀνωμαλία means irregularity or unevenness, so it can mean physical infirmity or illness. The English fixes it to "illness" and drops the vaguer sense of the source. The verb is also "be left behind", not "prevented".
last_rejected.fix: unless he is left behind by some disability or infirmity.
last_rejected.ruling: δι᾽ ἀνωμαλίαν normally includes bodily disorder, so “illness” is in range; ἀπολιμπάνοιτο as being kept away is fairly “prevented.”
